title: The Cascade of the New

sourceEvidence.locator: A hierarchy measured by available freedom
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The Cascade is a chain of realities nested within realities. Dimensional rank does not measure intelligence or moral worth; it measures how many freedoms a world can preserve. Three-dimensional people inhabit one body and an irreversible past. Higher beings may revisit histories, retain alternative futures, alter families of natural law, or maintain compatible versions of themselves. Every level can simulate simpler levels while remaining potentially simulated by something above.

sourceEvidence.locator: A hierarchy measured by available freedom
sourceEvidence.excerpt: This cosmology makes power intimate. A home may be a synchronized arrangement of histories rather than a building, and scarcity may erase possibilities rather than possessions. Interfaces called velars connect levels; continuity agreements called marns determine whether a descended person remains legally the same individual or becomes a disposable copy. The Valency allocates the New—unexpected, intelligible, consequential choices—to worlds where difference can continue. The arrangement sounds like stewardship until the lives generating that resource acquire voices.

sourceEvidence.locator: The Aster file and the economy of novelty
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Sera Vey audits cascades for the Recursive Continuity Nex and can authorize isolation, closure, or release. She begins amid personal scarcity: her own home must surrender cherished histories and unrealized relationships as the Valency withdraws support. Then the Aster cascade reaches her with evidence that its extraordinary novelty may have been engineered through suffering. Closure would end exploitation, but it would also extinguish the conscious worlds entangled in the system.

sourceEvidence.locator: The Aster file and the economy of novelty
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Her old ally Taal Or argues that eliminating danger can eliminate the freedom from which genuine novelty arises. His market is not based on money: forecasters stake possible versions of themselves, gaining possibilities when correct and losing branches when wrong. This gives prediction bodily cost while also making lives below into productive assets. The book's central pressure emerges here: administrators can measure crisis, innovation, and stability while discounting pain according to how far down the Cascade it occurs.

hook: Closing an exploited world might stop its suffering and erase everyone living there.
readerPromise: Enter a layered speculative investigation where protection and destruction become a personal administrative dilemma.
protectedRevelations: Discoveries during descent, inhabitants' fates, final decisions and wider cosmology.
visualPlan: A world on the closure list: Replace the later preserved-mother scene with an inhabited world beside an unchosen shutdown control. Sera receives the Aster case file with its affected world visible as a lived place.
The auditor must descend: Show an allegation in the case record without illustrating suffering or confirming the claim. Sera approaches the transfer threshold with the record still incomplete.
One vulnerable body: During descent, remove one optional path and keep Sera’s embodied support rail visible. Move to an ordinary desk and home detail belonging to someone inside the case.

What a file cannot contain: The case volume holds a meal, bodily need and testimony that exceed one official category. End with a finger following the case downward toward the inhabited scene, not its resolution.
